meta.title: WordLink-Edge Model Technical Report | Lexiverse
meta.description: Full-pipeline technical report on domain fine-tuning Qwen2.5-1.5B: diverse corpus engineering, SFT, DPO, Apple MPS training-stability engineering, and a 90-prompt measured benchmark.

hero.tagline: A 1.5B on-device model built for vocabulary teaching: a Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct base, domain-finetuned end to end with diverse-corpus SFT and DPO on real failure negatives — with all training done locally on Apple Silicon.
hero.taglineHighlight: Every number on this page is reproducible.
hero.period: Training window 2026-09-07 ~ 09-09 · Apple Silicon (48GB unified memory, MPS backend, no CUDA)
hero.evidence: The value of small-model fine-tuning (+25pp hit rate at the same scale, JSON 82%→100%) and scale-independent zero-shot failure (7B zero-shot: 39.72% hit / 0% JSON) together form the complete evidence chain for why domain fine-tuning is necessary. DPO is statistically on par with SFT (the difference lies within the n=90 noise band), with steadier behavioral convergence and zero reward-hacking regressions — it validates the safety of the alignment recipe, not metric-chasing.

task.title: Base model & task definition,
task.sub: Why 1.5B: it is the smallest engine that passes the quality bar in testing. The target form factor is in-browser on-device inference — works offline, zero marginal cost, and student data never leaves the device.

definition.label: Task definition
definition.value: CEFR-constrained micro-story generation: given a topic + 3~4 due review words + a level (A2/B1/B2), output a JSON-structured short story (title / body / Chinese translation / vocabulary notes) with target words bolded inline

target.label: Target form factor
target.value: In-browser WebGPU 4-bit on-device inference (~950MB; offline, zero marginal cost, data never leaves the device)

c1.d: Every due review word must be embedded naturally in the story

c2.d: An A2 learner never meets B2 vocabulary

c3.d: Readable in under a minute per session

c4.d: Output can be consumed programmatically as-is

data.title: Data engineering,
data.titleAccent: from template memorization to real generalization
data.sub: The v1 template corpus (510 entries, word-swap skeletons) taught SFT nothing but template memorization — the inflated 98.33% hit rate was itself evidence of overfitting, and the uninformative preference pairs left DPO spinning idle. v2 was rebuilt from scratch.

gen.title: Generation pipeline
gen.i1: · 44 topics × A2/B1/B2 × target word sets, generated by teacher model DeepSeek-V3
gen.i2: · 12-way concurrency, flushed to disk entry by entry, resumable from checkpoints
gen.i3: · chosen passes five hard filters: hit=1.0 and out-of-level=0 + valid JSON + length band 60~200 words + FKGL difficulty band (A2: 2.5-7.5 / B1: 5-10.5 / B2: 8-13.5)

neg.title: Negatives & evaluation hygiene
neg.i1: · rejected comes entirely from Qwen2.5-7B zero-shot (temperature 0.9) real failure outputs on the same prompts — collected only when hits are incomplete, vocabulary is out-of-level, or JSON is broken; no hand-crafted templates
neg.i2: · Failure modes include degenerate repetition and broken fields — far denser in information than synthetic negatives
neg.i3: · Deduplicated against the 90-prompt test set by prompt; the test set file was never modified
neg.i4: · Verifier: phrase normalization + lightweight lemmatization + exact word matching (fixes cat⊂category) + proper-noun exemption; deterministic with seed=42

sft.title: Supervised fine-tuning,
sft.sub: Target-word slot injection, CEFR boundary control, and structured JSON output. Control group: v1 template data converged in 93 steps at loss 0.029 — such a low loss is itself hard evidence of template memorization; v2's loss of 0.37 is the learning curve of real generalization.

hyper.label: Hyperparameters
hyper.value: lr 2e-4 cosine, warmup 3%, 3 epochs, batch 1 × accum 16, max_seq 896 (fixed-length padding, zero truncation)

precision.label: Precision
precision.value: fp32 (bf16 has an autocast memory leak on MPS and showed no speedup, so it was dropped)

dpo.title: Direct preference optimization,
dpo.sub: Statistically on par with SFT with zero regression — DPO's value lies in behavioral robustness (which shows under distribution shift), not benchmark gains. All four acceptance checks passed, proving the recipe neither idles nor reward-hacks.

start.label: Starting point
start.value: Base + SFT LoRA merged via merge_and_unload() (wordlink_edge_sft_v2_merged)

lora.label: DPO LoRA
lora.value: r=32, α=64, dropout=0.05, target=[q,v,o,gate,down]_proj (25.9M trainable parameters)

betaLr.label: β / LR
betaLr.value: 0.1 / 5e-6, cosine, warmup 5%, 2 epochs, batch 1 × accum 16, seed=42

data.label: Data
data.value: 2045 pairs (chosen = positives after five hard filters / rejected = real 7B zero-shot failure outputs)

guard.label: Safety valve
guard.value: NoOpGuard: throws if loss<1e-4 within the first 20 steps (prevents no-op training)

result.label: Result
result.value: 256/256 steps, all four acceptance checks passed: margins climbing 0.105→11.28 | loss converging 0.6438→0.0001 | adapter MD5≠SFT | chosen logps continuously changing

incident.eyebrow: ⚠ Engineering postmortem · the v1 DPO no-op incident
incident.intro: The first DPO run trained for 1 hour 47 minutes with zero weight change (adapter MD5 byte-identical to SFT). Two root causes:
incident.cause1Body: With ref_model=None and a PeftModel already carrying the SFT adapter, TRL 0.11 used the raw base with the adapter disabled as the reference model; β·margin≈6.4 saturated the sigmoid and gradients stayed zero (logs: loss=0 / grad_norm=0 / margins≈64).
incident.cause2Body: The old chosen was the SFT training template and rejected was a fixed sentence, so margins were huge by construction after SFT and preference learning never happened.
incident.fix: Fix: merge → fresh LoRA → NoOpGuard fail-fast. Both root causes are fixed and accepted in v2. Also note: the DPO adapter must be loaded on top of the merged base+ΔSFT model; attaching it to the raw base only reaches ≈base-level scores (63.89% — a trap verified by measurement).

mps.title: Apple MPS training stability,
mps.sub: Completing the full real training pipeline on a 48GB unified-memory Mac without CUDA took a whole set of platform-level workarounds. The segmented-resume scheme is now codified as an orchestrator plus watchdog, running hundreds of steps unattended.

leak.s: Memory grows ~1.4GB/step in long single-process runs, independent of precision, batch size, grouping, or GC frequency
leak.f: Platform-level issue in the torch MPS backend → segmented resume: checkpoint and exit every 117/128 steps, relaunch a fresh process from the checkpoint, orchestrator loops until done

denominator.f: The denominator of set_per_process_memory_fraction is the system-recommended 37.4GB, not the physical 48GB → recompute the watermark against the true denominator

fragmentation.s: Tensor shapes differ every step; allocator cache reuse is zero
fragmentation.f: batch=1 + continuously distributed lengths (636~891 tok) → fixed-length padding (896, zero truncation)

bf16.s: bf16 adds a net 1.2GB per step
bf16.f: torch 2.5.1 MPS autocast → dropped bf16 for fp32 (no measured speed difference)

crash.f: Hard ceiling guardrails → checkpoint every 40 steps + watchdog auto-resume; loss bounded to ≤40 steps

bench.title: Final measured results,
bench.titleAccent: 90 prompts · greedy decoding · scored from real outputs
bench.sub: All metrics are computed by an automated evaluator on the model's real generations (temperature=0); evaluation details and per-prompt outputs live in the repo under outputs/eval/. Target-word hit = share of due review words naturally embedded in the story; out-of-level = share of vocabulary beyond the target CEFR level.

dpo.name: + DPO preference alignment (v2)
dpo.note: On par with SFT, steadier behavior

bench.footnote: * The 7B zero-shot failure is independent of sampling parameters: a rerun with anti-degeneracy leniency still scored 41.67% / 0% JSON. Fine-tuning lets the 1.5B approach the DeepSeek-V3 teacher on the same task (88.06% vs 97.78%; the remaining gap is mainly rhetorical quality in long, complex sentences) and far surpasses an unfine-tuned model 4.7× its size.

n1.d: near-miss negatives (almost-right outputs off by a single word) + a larger test set (500 prompts) + multi-seed confidence intervals

n2.d: MLC/WebLLM 4-bit export (compile_mlc.sh, requires the mlc-llm toolchain) or a one-click GPU-server pipeline

n3.d: Mixed generation with a second teacher to improve stylistic diversity
